crossRefs.note: They drive away the donkey of the fatherless, and they take the widow’s ox for a pledge.
There are those who pluck the fatherless from the breast, and take a pledge of the poor,
If you take your neighbor’s garment as collateral, you shall restore it to him before the sun goes down,
When you lend your neighbor any kind of loan, you shall not go into his house to get his pledge.
and has not wronged any, but has restored to the debtor his pledge, has taken nothing by robbery, has given his bread…

hasn’t wronged any, hasn’t taken anything to pledge, hasn’t taken by robbery, but has given his bread to the hungry…

translations.web: For you have taken pledges from your brother for nothing, and stripped the naked of their clothing.
translations.bsb: For you needlessly demanded security from your brothers and deprived the naked of their clothing.
translations.kjv: For thou hast taken a pledge from thy brother for nought, and stripped the naked of their clothing.
translations.asv: For thou hast taken pledges of thy brother for nought, And stripped the naked of their clothing.
